In January 1839 forces of the East India Company seized the port of Aden in southern Yemen. Britain held it for 128 years, until 1967.

Aden was wanted as a coaling station for steamships on the route to India. After the Suez Canal opened in 1869 it became one of the busiest ports in the world, with a refinery and a mixed population of Arabs, Indians, Somalis and Jews. Britain also signed protection treaties with the sultans of the hinterland, the Aden Protectorate.

The British border between Aden's hinterland and the Ottoman north split Yemen in two for most of the 20th century. British rule ended in the Aden Emergency, and the south became South Yemen.
sum: In January 1839 forces of the East India Company seized the port of Aden in southern Yemen. Britain held it for 128 years, until 1967.
